Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Vendor X)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned with OmniHealth’s evaluation criteria.

Summary of what we heard (pain points / goals):
- Latency spikes on peak traffic (ER workflows) lead to timeouts and clinician friction — target P95 < 300ms for short prompts.
- Cost predictability: procurement needs predictable unit economics for a monthly committed plan.
- Data controls & audit: SOC2, KMS for key management, and retention/audit logs are gating items.
- Model quality: want to measure hallucination rate on discharge summaries and correctness on structured extraction.

How Redwood maps to those items: 
- Serving runtime: designed for consistent P95s via continuous batching + KV cache — we’ve included preliminary latency profiles in the attached bake-off plan.
- Cost controls: Dedicated capacity options with commit pricing; Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Compliance: Private deployment option (VPC + on-prem package) + audit logs and KMS integrations.

Open questions we captured:
1) Which endpoints/workloads are highest priority for the bake-off? (ER triage vs discharge summaries vs scheduling)
2) What size of dataset will you provide for hallucination/regression tests?
3) Any procurement constraints on test environments (IP allowlist, port rules)?

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to run a focused latency & cost simulation against a representative prompt set (we’ll need ~200 sample prompts + traffic profile).
- Redwood SE (Aditya) to provide a short test plan and CSV template for results.
- Schedule 2-hour technical bake-off session the week of Apr 19 — participant suggestions: Marissa (CSM), Aditya (SE), Rishi (Solution Architect), OmniHealth engineers + procurement.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf (1 page, plan + test matrix)

Please confirm the top-2 workloads you want in the bake-off and whether Apr 20 or Apr 21 works for the technical session.

Thanks —
Marissa

- 2) ER triage prompts (latency-critical)

Dataset: we can provide ~500 annotated discharge summaries and 1,000 short ER prompts with expected answers. Can you confirm the format you prefer (CSV / JSONL)?

- Can you run the latency sim against both Dedicated and Hosted variants so we can compare cost/latency tradeoffs?
- For hallucination testing, do you support automatic metric calculation (F1 / BLEU / hallucination flagging) or should we run locally on our side?

Hi Samantha —

We can take the CSV or JSONL — CSV with columns (prompt, expected_output, tags) is easiest for our ingestion. I attached a small results CSV from an internal latency run to show the format we’ll deliver.

Answers to your questions: 
- We will run latency/cost sims on both Hosted and Dedicated. The plan: a) synthetic replay for traffic profile to estimate P95 and cost; b) isolated Dedicated run for sustained throughput to show tail behavior.
- For hallucination metrics: Redwood Optimize can run automated evals (we calculate precision/F1 and simple hallucination heuristics). If you prefer, we can run the metrics and share raw outputs so OmniHealth can re-run locally.

Proposed technical bake-off test cases (short):
1) Discharge summary QA: 500 examples, measure F1 and hallucination rate.
2) ER triage latency: 1,000 short prompts at burst QPS patterns, measure P50/P95/P99 across Hosted vs Dedicated.

We’ll need the following from OmniHealth before the run:
- Pseudonymized sample CSV (500 discharges, 1,000 ER prompts)
- Traffic profile (average QPS, peak QPS, typical prompt length)
- IP allowlist for test VPC access (if Dedicated test required)

Attachments: kv-cache-results.csv (sample latency results)

I’ll prepare the test script and share a link to a Google Drive folder with templates by EOD.

—Aditya
